subject: Unexpected February overage — request for breakdown and provisional credit
messages:
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Spike in January->Feb billing — unexpected overage

Hi Soojin / Marcus,

We noticed a large jump on our February invoice compared to our January baseline — roughly +42% token consumption month-over-month. Attached is a small export from our side (acme-usage-sample.csv) showing session ids, endpoints called, and timestamps for a 48-hour window (attached). Can you confirm how those calls would be metered on your side and whether there was any change on Redwood's metering logic or model mapping in late Jan?

Key asks:
- Line-item breakdown by model + route for the attached window
- Any recent change to tokenizer/kernel selection that could affect token counts
- Whether retried/duplicated requests are deduplicated from billing

We have a PO on file and were concerned about the size of the overage. If this turns out to be an anomaly on Redwood's side wed like to request a provisional credit while you investigate.

Thanks,
Tom
Billing Ops | Acme Corp
Phone: +1-415-555-0123

Attachment: acme-usage-sample.csv (CSV, 12KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 16:10:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in January->Feb billing — unexpected overage

Tom — thanks for the export, that helps. Im escalating to billing ops and our runtime team for a root-cause audit. Initial responses below.

What were going to do immediately:
- Run a backend metering export for the exact session ids/time window you provided (will attach CSV)
- Provide a model-by-endpoint reconciliation and tokenization previews for a sample of requests
- Check recent deploys (kernel/quantization changes) between 2027-01-20 and 2027-02-05

Naomi (cc) will run the billing export — Naomi, can you add the per-token breakdown and a note on whether retries are deduplicated?

Separately, we can consider a provisional credit while the audit runs. Marcus, can you estimate the typical turnaround for an audit like this?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-metering-extract-202701.csv (CSV, 95KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 17:05:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in January->Feb billing — unexpected overage

Putting together a quick hypothesis from the telemetry: were seeing a cluster of calls to your /embed/bulk endpoint that were re-ingests of a daily index job. A few operational notes:

- Bulk embedding jobs that batch many items can cause per-call tokenization variance (prefixes + repeated prompts). If the job changed to include a longer system prompt or a new metadata prefix, that could account for the jump.
- Our metering deduplicates identical request ids (x-request-id) but not logically equivalent requests with different session ids.
- We did a runtime kernel rollout on 2027-01-25 for better memory packing; that change should not affect token counting but can change model selection heuristics in rare cases.

Next steps Ill run:
1) Produce a per-request token trace for the session ids in your CSV (will attach trace CSV).
2) Cross-check request headers for duplicate ids; flag any retries.
3) If the traces point to a prompt-change in your ingestion pipeline, well mark those tokens as customer-initiated. If it looks like double-ingestion on our side, we propose a provisional credit for the disputed window.

ETA: preliminary export in ~8 hours, full audit in 48 hours.

- Marcus
Principal SRE, Runtime
Attachment: redwood-request-trace-20270209.csv (CSV, 48KB)
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-corp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in January->Feb billing — unexpected overage

Thanks Soojin / Marcus — quick clarification: the ingestion pipeline did not change in January, and the system prompt length was constant per our internal changelog. The only operational change was a temporary ramp-up of the daily re-index job to catch up after an internal failure on Feb 1. Ive attached our own aggregation of top endpoints and timestamps (see top_endpoints_snapshot.csv).

Two requests:
1) Can Redwood share the CSV from the metering export as soon as its ready? Well reconcile on our side.
2) Given the business impact, can Redwood issue a provisional credit for the disputed amount while the audit completes? Were happy to sign a statement-of-facts if that helps.

PO reference: PO-ACME-7782
Billing contact for payment holds: elena.ruiz@acme-corp.com

Tom

Attachment: top_endpoints_snapshot.csv (CSV, 18KB)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spike in January->Feb billing — unexpected overage

Tom / Elena — quick update and proposed resolution path.

Summary of findings so far (preliminary):
- Naomis metering export shows a concentrated set of spikes on 2027-02-02 between 03:00-06:00 UTC for your project id. Those calls are all to /embed/bulk with higher-than-normal token counts driven by repeated metadata prefixes.
- Marcuss traces confirm the requests were ingested with distinct session ids; we do not see evidence of Redwood-triggered duplicate replays in our service logs.

Proposed interim resolution:
- Redwood will grant a one-time provisional credit equal to 50% of the disputed overage while we complete the full 48-hour audit. This is subject to final reconciliation; if the audit shows the extra tokens are customer-initiated, the credit will be rebalanced on the next invoice.
- We will deliver the full audit report (CSV + reconciliation notes) by EOD Friday, 2027-02-12.
- If you prefer a formal statement-of-facts for your AP team, we can provide one after the audit.

Please confirm that provisional 50% credit is acceptable and whether you want the credit applied now or reserved pending final reconciliation. If you want the credit now well route to Billing for immediate application (usually appears as invoice credit within 2 business days).

Thanks for the quick context — well keep you posted.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
